```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_preterm"))$reference`
* Description (preterm): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_preterm"))$description`
* Description (term): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_term"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2022.977372> (open access)

Zazo et al. built a minimal physiologically based PK (PBPK) model of
gentamicin in neonates in the PhysPK / EcosimPro platform. It has four
states: serum, a well-stirred heart chamber perfused by the cardiac output,
a flow-limited kidney that eliminates the drug, and a flow-limited "rest of
tissues" pool. Every parameter came from the literature; nothing was fitted.
Between-subject variability is a log-normal Monte Carlo over body weight,
glomerular filtration rate (GFR), serum volume of distribution, cardiac
output and kidney blood flow. The authors used one structure with two sets
of physiological values, one for preterm and one for term neonates, so the
package ships two model files that share this vignette.

**Read the Errata section before using these models.** Built from the
printed equations and tables, the model reproduces the paper's clearance
but not its concentrations. Simulated serum concentrations at 2 h are
roughly 30-40% below the paper's own predictions in Table 4 and Figure 2.

# Population

Source paper Table 3: 47 neonates in the first week of life, treated at the
University Hospital of Salamanca (Spain) between 1999 and 2003 and monitored
by routine TDM, with 91 serum samples taken 2 and 24 h after the start of
the infusion.

* Preterm (gestational age 32-37 weeks, n = 31): body weight
  1.96 +/- 0.41 kg, postnatal age 3.03 +/- 1.02 days, dose
  5.74 +/- 0.80 mg/kg every 48 h.
* Term (gestational age 38-39 weeks, n = 16): body weight
  3.09 +/- 0.23 kg, postnatal age 2.94 +/- 0.85 days, dose
  6.64 +/- 0.22 mg/kg every 36 h.

These patients validated the model; they were not used to fit it. Sex
distribution is not reported. The same information is available
programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_preterm")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Preterm | Term | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| `d/dt(heart_chamber)` | -- | -- | Eq. 1 |
| `d/dt(kidney)` | -- | -- | Eq. 2 |
| `qe <- WT * gfr * 0.79` | -- | -- | Eq. 3 (21% tubular reabsorption) |
| `d/dt(other)` | -- | -- | Eq. 4 |
| `d/dt(central)` | -- | -- | Eq. 5, corrected (see Errata) |
| `cl <- q_kidney * qe / (q_kidney + qe)` | -- | -- | steady-state clearance of the Eq. 2-3 kidney; compared with Table 4 CL |
| `lvc` (serum Vd, L/kg) | median of 0.52 +/- 0.16 | median of 0.46 +/- 0.14 | Table 2 |
| `lgfr` (mL/min/kg) | median of 1.31 +/- 0.53 (= 1.21) | median of 1.72 +/- 0.70 (= 1.59) | Table 2; medians quoted in the Discussion |
| `lqc` (cardiac output, mL/min/kg) | median of 172 +/- 50.6 | same | Table 2 |
| `lq_kidney` (mL/min/kg) | median of 9.35, CV 20% | same | Table 1; CV in section 2.1.3 |
| `lq_other` (mL/min/kg) | 217 | same | Table 1 |
| `lv_kidney` (mL) | 0.03 | same | Table 1 |
| `lv_other` (mL) | 0.87 | same | Table 1 |
| `lkp_kidney` | 10.0 | same | Table 1 |
| `lkp_other` | 1.00 | same | Table 1 |
| `lv_heart_chamber` (mL) | 5 | same | **not in the paper**; assumed by the maintainers |
| `etalvc` | CV 30.8% | CV 30.4% | Table 2 SD / mean |
| `etalgfr` | CV 40.5% | CV 40.7% | Table 2 SD / mean (section 2.1.3: 40%) |
| `etalq_kidney` | CV 20% | same | section 2.1.3 |
| `etalqc` | CV 29.4% | same | Table 2 SD / mean (section 2.1.3: 24%) |
| `WT` (body weight, kg) | 1.73 +/- 0.35 | 3.56 +/- 0.72 | Table 2 (Monte Carlo); CV 20% in section 2.1.3 |

Each Monte Carlo parameter is reported as an arithmetic mean +/- SD of a
log-normal distribution. The `ini()` value is the log-normal median,
`mean / sqrt(1 + CV^2)`, and the variance is `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The
paper confirms this reading for GFR: the Discussion quotes the implemented
GFR values as 1.21 and 1.59 mL/min/kg. Those are exactly the log-normal
medians of Table 2's 1.31 +/- 0.53 and 1.72 +/- 0.70. The 40% CV in the text
would instead give 1.60 for term neonates.

# Structural checks

```{r models}
mod_pre <- readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_preterm")
mod_term <- readModelDb("Zazo_2022_gentamicin_term")
typ_pre <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pre)
typ_term <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_term)
```

## Mass balance of the corrected serum equation

With filtration switched off (`lgfr` set to a negligible value), the four
states must hold the whole dose forever. Both sides of the check come from
the same solve, so a tight bound applies.

```{r mass-balance}
ev_mb <- rxode2::et(amt = 6 * 1.96, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(1, 6, 24))
no_elim <- typ_pre |> rxode2::ini(lgfr = log(1e-12))
mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(no_elim, ev_mb, params = c(WT = 1.96),
                      rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(total = central + heart_chamber + kidney + other)
knitr::kable(mb[, c("time", "central", "heart_chamber", "kidney", "other", "total")],
             digits = 6, caption = "Amounts (mg) with elimination switched off; dose 11.76 mg.")
stopifnot(max(abs(mb$total / (6 * 1.96) - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

The serum equation as printed (Eq. 5) has no `-(Qk + Qr) * Cb` term. The
tissues take up drug from serum (Eqs. 2 and 4) and return it, but the serum
never loses what they take up, so every pass through a tissue creates drug.
Replacing the corrected line with the printed one shows the consequence:

```{r literal-eq5}
literal <- typ_pre |>
  rxode2::model(d/dt(central) <- qc * c_heart_chamber + q_kidney * c_kidney / kp_kidney +
                  q_other * c_other / kp_other - qc * Cc)
ev_lit <- rxode2::et(amt = 6 * 1.96, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(c(0.25, 0.5, 1))
lit <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(literal, ev_lit, params = c(WT = 1.96))) |>
  as.data.frame()
cor <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ_pre, ev_lit, params = c(WT = 1.96)) |> as.data.frame()
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(time = cor$time, corrected = cor$Cc, printed = lit$Cc),
  digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  caption = "Typical preterm serum concentration (mg/L), corrected vs. printed Eq. 5."
)
stopifnot(all(lit$Cc[lit$time == 1] > 100 * cor$Cc[cor$time == 1]))
```

## Peak bound

Gentamicin is infused into serum and the tissues are tiny (see Errata), so
the serum concentration can never exceed dose / Vd. Table 2 sets Vd at
0.52 L/kg (preterm) and 0.46 L/kg (term), which caps the peak after
6 mg/kg near 11.5 and 13 mg/L. The paper's Table 4 mean C2h of 17.4 and
15.4 mg/L sit above that cap.

```{r peak-bound}
peak_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(list(list("Preterm", typ_pre, 1.96), list("Term", typ_term, 3.09)), function(g) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 6 * g[[3]], dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(seq(0, 4, by = 0.05))
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(g[[2]], ev, params = c(WT = g[[3]])) |> as.data.frame()
  vd <- exp(rxode2::rxode(g[[2]])$theta[["lvc"]]) * g[[3]]
  data.frame(group = g[[1]], cmax = max(s$Cc), bound = 6 * g[[3]] / vd)
}))
knitr::kable(peak_tbl, digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical-value peak (mg/L) vs. dose / Vd at the Table 3 mean weight.")
stopifnot(all(peak_tbl$cmax <= peak_tbl$bound * (1 + 1e-6)))
```

## Heart-chamber volume sensitivity

The paper does not print the heart-chamber volume `Vh`; it is a built-in
value of the PhysPK platform. The models carry an assumed 5 mL. Varying it
100-fold shows how little it matters:

```{r vh-sensitivity}
vh_tbl <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0.5, 5, 50), function(vh) {
  bind_rows(lapply(list(list("Preterm", typ_pre, 1.96), list("Term", typ_term, 3.09)), function(g) {
    m <- g[[2]] |> rxode2::ini(lv_heart_chamber = log(vh))
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 6 * g[[3]], dur = 0.5, cmt = "central") |> rxode2::et(c(2, 24))
    s <- suppressMessages(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev, params = c(WT = g[[3]]))) |> as.data.frame()
    data.frame(group = g[[1]], vh_mL = vh, C2h = s$Cc[s$time == 2], C24h = s$Cc[s$time == 24])
  }))
}))
vh_tbl <- vh_tbl |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(C2h_change_pct = 100 * (C2h / C2h[vh_mL == 5] - 1),
         C24h_change_pct = 100 * (C24h / C24h[vh_mL == 5] - 1)) |>
  ungroup()
knitr::kable(vh_tbl, digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical-value C2h and C24h (mg/L) by assumed heart-chamber volume.")
```

From 0.5 to 5 mL, C2h and C24h move by under 1%. A 50 mL chamber, close to
half of a preterm neonate's total blood volume, moves C2h by under 5% and
C24h by under 15%. Even then, none of the concentration gap in the
comparison below is closed.

# Virtual cohorts

The paper's Monte Carlo drew 1,000 virtual patients per group with body
weight from Table 2. The cohorts below use 200 per group. The Figure 2 and
Table 5 cohorts follow the paper's Monte Carlo, with weight drawn
log-normally from Table 2. The Table 4 clearance comparison uses the
observed Table 3 weights, because the paper compares predicted with observed
patient clearance (see Errata).

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20221)
set.seed(20221)

draw_lognormal <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  cv <- sd / mean
  mean / sqrt(1 + cv^2) * exp(rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(log(1 + cv^2))))
}

make_cohort <- function(n, wt_mean, wt_sd, dose_mgkg, obs_times, id_offset) {
  subj <- tibble(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), WT = draw_lognormal(n, wt_mean, wt_sd))
  dose <- subj |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_mgkg * WT, dur = 0.5, cmt = "central")
  obs <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = NA_real_, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

grid <- seq(0, 72, by = 0.25)
n_arm <- 200L

cohorts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~regimen,              ~dose, ~tau, ~wt_mean, ~wt_sd, ~offset,
  "Preterm", "Extended 6 mg/kg q48h",  6,  48,   1.73,     0.35,      0L,
  "Preterm", "Conventional 4 mg/kg q24h", 4, 24, 1.73,     0.35,    200L,
  "Term",    "Extended 6 mg/kg q36h",  6,  36,   3.56,     0.72,    400L,
  "Term",    "Conventional 4 mg/kg q24h", 4, 24, 3.56,     0.72,    600L,
  "Preterm", "Patients (Table 3 weight)", 6, 48, 1.96,     0.41,    800L,
  "Term",    "Patients (Table 3 weight)", 6, 36, 3.09,     0.23,   1000L
)

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cohorts)), function(i) {
  cohorts[i, ] |>
    with(make_cohort(n_arm, wt_mean, wt_sd, dose, grid, offset)) |>
    mutate(group = cohorts$group[i], regimen = cohorts$regimen[i], tau = cohorts$tau[i])
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

Each group is solved with its own model file. Only the first dosing interval
is used: the paper's samples (2 and 24 h after the first dose) and its VPC
cover the first interval.

```{r simulate}
sim <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pre, events = filter(events, group == "Preterm"),
                  keep = c("group", "regimen", "tau", "WT")) |> as.data.frame(),
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_term, events = filter(events, group == "Term"),
                  keep = c("group", "regimen", "tau", "WT")) |> as.data.frame()
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

# Figure 2: visual predictive check

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
observed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~time, ~mean, ~sd,
  "Preterm",     2, 17.7,  4.28,
  "Preterm",    24, 2.92,  0.79,
  "Term",        2, 13.8,  3.08,
  "Term",       24, 1.41,  0.41
)
published_pred <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~time, ~mean,
  "Preterm",     2, 17.4,
  "Preterm",    24, 2.62,
  "Term",        2, 15.4,
  "Term",       24, 0.89
)

vpc <- sim |>
  filter(grepl("Extended", regimen), time <= tau) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25), q50 = median(Cc),
            q75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(data = observed, aes(y = mean, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd),
                  colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = published_pred, aes(y = mean), shape = 4, size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Time after start of first infusion (h)", y = "Serum gentamicin (mg/L)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2 of Zazo 2022 (6 mg/kg; 90% and 50% intervals).",
                       "Blue: observed mean +/- SD (Table 3). Red cross: published",
                       "model-predicted mean (Table 4)."))
```

The simulated median peaks near 11-13 mg/L at the end of the infusion. The
paper's Figure 2 median peaks at about 22 mg/L. The observed 2-h concentrations (blue) sit well above the
simulated median: the printed model does not reproduce its own VPC.

# Table 4: concentrations and clearance

```{r table-4}
cl_cmp <- sim |>
  filter(regimen == "Patients (Table 3 weight)") |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    C2h = mean(Cc[time == 2]),
    C24h = mean(Cc[time == 24]),
    CL = mean(cl[time == 0]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(source = "Simulated (Table 3 weights)")

mc_conc <- sim |>
  filter(grepl("Extended", regimen)) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(C2h = mean(Cc[time == 2]), C24h = mean(Cc[time == 24]),
            CL = mean(cl[time == 0]), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(source = "Simulated (Table 2 weights)")

pub4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~C2h, ~C24h, ~CL,
  "Preterm", 17.4, 2.62,  0.11,
  "Term",    15.4, 0.89,  0.23
) |> mutate(source = "Published prediction (Table 4)")
obs4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~C2h, ~C24h, ~CL,
  "Preterm", 17.7, 2.92,  0.09,
  "Term",    13.8, 1.41,  0.19
) |> mutate(source = "Observed (Table 4)")

bind_rows(cl_cmp, mc_conc, pub4, obs4) |>
  arrange(group, source) |>
  dplyr::rename("Group" = group, "Source" = source, "C2h (mg/L)" = C2h,
                "C24h (mg/L)" = C24h, "CL (L/h)" = CL) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean values, simulated vs. Zazo 2022 Table 4.")

# Clearance reproduces Table 4. CL is an algebraic function of the drawn
# physiology, so the 200-subject mean has a sampling SE near 3%; a
# mis-transcribed GFR, kidney flow or reabsorption factor moves it by far more.
cl_ratio <- cl_cmp$CL / pub4$CL[match(cl_cmp$group, pub4$group)]
stopifnot(all(abs(cl_ratio - 1) < 0.2))
```

Clearance reproduces Table 4 to within about 10%. That is the model's
reusable result: a flow-limited kidney with elimination flow
`TBW * GFR * 0.79` predicts neonatal gentamicin clearance from GFR alone.
The concentrations do not reproduce. Simulated C2h is about 40% (preterm)
and a third (term) below the published predictions, and below the observed
means. C24h is also below the published predictions. This is a known deviation of the printed model, not a simulation
artifact (see the peak bound above), so no assertion is placed on it.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(regimen == "Patients (Table 3 weight)", !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(sim_nca, sim_nca |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)) |>
  distinct(id, group, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, group, time)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, regimen == "Patients (Table 3 weight)") |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id, route = "intravascular",
                             duration = 0.5)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~cl.obs,
  "Preterm", 0.11,
  "Term",    0.23
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cl.obs = "L/h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "PKNCA clearance (dose / AUC0-inf) vs. Table 4 predicted CL. * differs by >20%.")
```

The paper reports no Cmax, AUC or half-life, so clearance is the only NCA
quantity with a published counterpart. The full PKNCA summary follows for
reference:

```{r pknca-summary}
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res), caption = "PKNCA summary, 6 mg/kg single dose, Table 3 weights.")
```

# Table 5: probability of target attainment

The target criteria come from source paper section 2.5, with MIC 1 mg/L. The
efficacy targets are Cmax/MIC >= 8 and time above MIC >= 60% of the dosing
interval. The toxicity targets are Cmin >= 2 mg/L and Cmax >= 25 mg/L. All
four are evaluated over the first dosing interval.

```{r table-5}
pta <- sim |>
  filter(!grepl("Patients", regimen), time <= tau) |>
  group_by(group, regimen, id) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), cmin = Cc[time == tau[1]],
            tmic = mean(Cc[time < tau[1]] > 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(group, regimen) |>
  summarise(`Cmax/MIC >= 8` = 100 * mean(cmax >= 8),
            `T>MIC >= 60%` = 100 * mean(tmic >= 0.6),
            `Cmin >= 2 mg/L` = 100 * mean(cmin >= 2),
            `Cmax >= 25 mg/L` = 100 * mean(cmax >= 25),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(source = "Simulated")
pub5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~regimen,                    ~`Cmax/MIC >= 8`, ~`T>MIC >= 60%`, ~`Cmin >= 2 mg/L`, ~`Cmax >= 25 mg/L`,
  "Preterm", "Conventional 4 mg/kg q24h", 10.8,             87.9,            5.0,               0.0,
  "Preterm", "Extended 6 mg/kg q48h",     99.9,             70.7,            5.9,               6.9,
  "Term",    "Conventional 4 mg/kg q24h", 32.3,             61.2,            0.4,               0.0,
  "Term",    "Extended 6 mg/kg q36h",     99.8,             54.9,            1.8,               6.5
) |> mutate(source = "Published (Table 5)")
bind_rows(pta, pub5) |>
  arrange(group, regimen, source) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "PTA (%) at MIC 1 mg/L, simulated vs. Zazo 2022 Table 5.")
```

The extended-regimen attainments follow the concentration shortfall. Only
neonates with a low drawn Vd reach the 25 mg/L toxicity threshold, a few
percent at most against about 7% in Table 5. Time above MIC is also well
below the published value. The conventional regimen goes the other way: the
model's Cmax/MIC >= 8 attainment is higher than Table 5's. Errata item 7
explains why no linear model with log-normally distributed peaks can match
Table 5 in full.

# Assumptions and deviations

## Errata in the source

1. **Eq. 5 is not mass-conserving as printed.** The serum equation
   `Vd dCb/dt = G P(t) + Qh Ch + sum(Qi Ci / Pi) - Qh Cb` omits the
   `-sum(Qi) Cb` outflow to the kidney and rest of tissues that Eqs. 2 and 4
   take up. The models encode the corrected form. PhysPK generates the blood
   connections itself (section 2.2), so the printed equation is a summary
   of that code, not the code itself. The correction is the only reading in
   which the model conserves drug mass (see the mass-balance check above).
2. **Concentrations do not reproduce.** With the printed values, simulated
   C2h is about 30-40% below the paper's Table 4 predictions and its
   Figure 2 VPC median. Serum Vd from Table 2 (0.52 / 0.46 L/kg) bounds the
   peak at dose / Vd, roughly 11.5 / 13 mg/L after 6 mg/kg. The Figure 2
   peak of about 22 mg/L implies an apparent volume near 0.27 L/kg. No
   reading of the organ-volume units closes the gap. Larger tissue volumes
   only lower the peak further. Halving Vd alone, with clearance held at
   its Table 4 value, collapses C24h far below the observed values. The
   maintainers ship the printed values unchanged and do not tune them. The
   PhysPK model file is not published, and no supplement accompanies the
   article.
3. **Organ-volume units in Table 1.** Table 1 labels its organ volumes
   "(ml)" with values 0.03 (kidney) and 0.87 (rest of tissues). Read
   literally these are far below neonatal physiology, and they look like
   L/kg or fractions of body weight. They are encoded as printed (mL),
   which leaves the tissues with negligible drug-holding capacity. Reading
   them as L or L/kg lowers the simulated peak further, so the literal
   reading is also the one closest to the published concentrations. To
   test another reading, override `lv_kidney` / `lv_other` with
   `rxode2::ini()`.
4. **Kidney blood flow.** Section 2.1.3 says the kidney flow is in Table 2,
   but Table 2 has no such row. The models use Table 1's 9.35 mL/min/kg with
   the 20% CV stated in section 2.1.3. Table 1's rest-of-tissues flow
   (217 mL/min/kg) also exceeds the cardiac output (172 mL/min/kg). In this
   topology the heart chamber is a parallel recirculation loop, so the
   tissue flows are not drawn from the cardiac output, and the printed
   values are used as they are.
5. **Cardiac-output variability.** Section 2.1.3 gives the cardiac-output CV
   as 24%. Table 2 gives 172 +/- 50.6 mL/min/kg, a CV of 29.4%. The models
   use Table 2, which is the table of implemented values. For GFR, the
   Discussion's 1.21 / 1.59 medians match Table 2's SD (1.59) better than
   the text's 40% CV (1.60). Cardiac output only drives the heart-chamber
   loop, so the choice has no visible effect on serum concentrations.
6. **Term dose range.** Table 3 prints the term dose range as
   "6.99 - 6.21" mg/kg, reversed relative to the other rows. It is shown as
   printed in the population metadata.
7. **Table 5 peak attainments contradict each other.** The model is linear,
   so a neonate's peak after 6 mg/kg is 1.5 times its peak after 4 mg/kg.
   For preterm neonates, Table 5 has 89.2% of 4 mg/kg peaks below 8 mg/L
   and 99.9% of 6 mg/kg peaks at or above 8 mg/L. That puts 4 mg/kg peaks
   at or above 5.3 mg/L in 99.9% of neonates. So 89% of the 4 mg/kg peaks
   must lie between 5.3 and 8 mg/L. Yet 6.9% of 6 mg/kg peaks reach
   25 mg/L, which needs a 4 mg/kg peak of 16.7 mg/L or more. A log-normal
   peak that fits the first two figures puts essentially no neonate above
   16.7 mg/L. No single log-normal peak distribution satisfies all three
   figures, so the comparison above is descriptive only.

## Non-paper-derived values

* **Heart-chamber volume `Vh` = 5 mL** is assumed by the maintainers. The
  paper uses `Vh` in Eq. 1 but never gives a value (it is a PhysPK
  built-in). The sensitivity table above shows that a 0.5-50 mL range
  leaves the conclusions unchanged.
* **No residual error.** The paper's Monte Carlo varied physiology only, so
  `propSd` is held at zero.

## Other modelling choices

* The 30-min infusion pulse `G P(t)` of Eq. 5 is supplied by the dosing
  record (`dur = 0.5`, `cmt = "central"`) rather than written into the ODE.
* Body weight is a covariate (`WT`), not a random effect. The paper's
  log-normal TBW draw (Table 2, CV 20%) is reproduced in the virtual cohort.
* The paper notes that the Monte Carlo draws were uncorrelated; the
  models carry a diagonal OMEGA.
* The PTA comparison uses the first dosing interval. The paper does not
  say whether Table 5 used the first interval or steady state.
* The paper also estimated GFR with the PhysPK estimation module
  (1.176 +/- 0.037 and 1.324 +/- 0.054 mL/min/kg). Those values were a
  software check and are not part of the model.
